# Startup readback: AI-39

Contract version: 1

## Objective and acceptance outcomes

Remaining work is to turn the existing bounded Procurement launch into a requirement-first, evidence-backed comparison with durable decision records. Acceptance outcomes: hard requirements filter candidates before ranking and unknown compatibility remains unresolved; current item, delivery and required accessory costs plus source/retrieval freshness and review uncertainty are represented explicitly; a revised saved requirement creates a linked new comparison while retaining the previous decision and evidence; any purchase/payment request stops before execution.

## Dependencies and relevant contracts

AI-15, AI-16 and AI-19 are Done. Existing entry points are the Procurement page and `OnDemandLaunchForm`, `/api/workflows/launch` and `workflow-launch`; existing storage includes `on_demand_research_runs`, `research_sources` and `procurement_recommendations`, with canonical run/report/evidence handling from AI-15/19. Procurement owns requirements, research, comparisons and lifecycle; Finance may support affordability. Integration: Using existing `workflow-launch`, on-demand run, source/evidence and report contracts; integration risks: AI-01, DB-03, DB-05, EDGE-01, ACC-01, ACC-02, OPS-01, PROC-01 and WORKFLOW-01.

## Implementation and boundaries

Follow the three root specs: explicit requirements and decisive trade-offs, current cited evidence, freshness/uncertainty labels, and comparison grids; no popularity-first ranking and no autonomous purchase. Preserve authenticated user ownership, AAL2/RLS, bounded spend/search/model policy, correlation, audit and redaction. Inspect all direct producers/consumers before changing their schema. If migrations are needed, check main and active sibling PR prefixes first and add forward-only migration(s); no migration prefix or shared integration-rule/ledger changes until coordinated with the parent.

## Local tests and commands

Target deterministic contracts for requirement extraction/validation, hard-filter-before-rank, unknown compatibility, all-in integer-minor-unit cost, source freshness/review quality, revision linkage/history preservation and buy-request denial. On this root-based branch, the actual producer → profile parser → `staging-status` → `staging-accept` contract and release-gate tests pass (38/38), manager-core tests pass (24/24), contracts tests pass (27/27), workflow-launch route tests pass (7/7), and Procurement Edge tests pass (2/2). Database, manager-core, contracts and web typechecks, Edge checks and formatting pass. `corepack pnpm qa:doctor --fix` is green; `corepack pnpm test:db` reset from the pre-AI-14 baseline, applied the candidate migration chain including `20261021131410_ai39_procurement_lifecycle.sql`, passed the AI-14 backfill fixture (4 assertions) and all database suites (29 files, 564 assertions), including `ai39_procurement_research.sql` (19 assertions). Its `environment:drift -- repo-local` check passed with no mismatches across 1323 public columns. PR CI is the hosted changed-surface gate.

## Hosted proof and readiness

AI-39 explicitly requires one real staging complex-comparison journey: persist requirements before ranking; show a noncompliant and unknown-compatible candidate correctly; compare all-in prices and conflicting sources; revise a requirement and retain provenance; persist selected rationale; and stop at a buy/payment request. The root release gate already selects and validates the dedicated Procurement profile. The live runner must leave its flat `ProcurementStagingAcceptanceEvidence` artifact intact for `staging-status`; that converter binds it to the deployed candidate and creates the nested acceptance consumed by `staging-accept`. A previous branch added a wrapper before this converter, so the next-release candidate adds a regression from the actual Procurement evidence schema through the strict profile parser and acceptance converter. Staging still requires an authenticated visible browser; wait for the parent's queue slot and operator checkpoint before any login/MFA. After merge, run the bounded affected Procurement production smoke.

## Delegation and blockers

One owner remains accountable for AI-39 through CI, staging, merge, smoke and Linear Done; no nested coding/reviewer agents. AI-15/16/19 are complete prerequisites and AI-39 blocks AI-40 and AI-52. The active release branch starts from root candidate `1537007aa3dc86248e22531d70a10c00ef5bbe01` and carries the Procurement implementation; it must pass its changed-surface/CI proofs before staging. Parent owns staging sequencing and the real browser/MFA checkpoint. Do not dispatch while another candidate holds the staging slot.
